meta.title: Owler — keeps watch over your scheduled jobs
meta.description: A Mac app that lists the jobs you run on launchd and records the result of every run. Investigate any run with Claude Code in Cursor or VS Code.

lead: Set them up and dig into the results
with Claude Code in Cursor or VS Code.
points: Set up and investigate in Cursor or VS Code

product.title: See last night's runs first thing in the morning.
product.statement: Morning tasks handed to AI, nightly backups: every run is recorded.
product.statementMuted: Investigate any of them with Claude Code in Cursor or VS Code.
product.label: Features

items.title: Run history
items.body: Start and end times, exit code and output, recorded for every run.

items.title: AI reports
items.body: When a job runs Claude Code, its last message is shown with the run.

items.title: Cursor and VS Code
items.body: Opens the job's folder in your editor and starts a Claude Code conversation there.

items.title: Set up with AI
items.body: Tell Claude Code what to run and when, and it registers the job.

items.title: Menu bar
items.body: The latest result of each job, with a count of failures.

install.title: Get started in three steps.

steps.title: Install
steps.body: Download the DMG and drag Owler into Applications. Homebrew is supported too.

steps.title: First launch
steps.body: Owler is not notarized by Apple, so the first launch is blocked. Click Open Anyway in System Settings → Privacy & Security.

steps.title: Add a job
steps.body: Click New Job at the bottom left of the window and talk it through with Claude Code.

install.accessibility: Owler asks for Accessibility access on first use. It needs it to bring the editor window to the front.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Owler runs the jobs you register on launchd and shows their records. That is all it does. The app has no server, no analytics and no account.

sections.title: What it reads and writes
sections.body: Job definitions, and the record and output of each run, live in ~/Library/Application Support/Owler. The launchd agents live in ~/Library/LaunchAgents. When a job runs claude -p, Owler looks for that folder's Claude Code transcript and reads the last message. To find the editor window, it reads the titles of Cursor and VS Code windows.

sections.title: Nothing leaves your Mac
sections.body: Every record stays on this Mac. Nothing is collected and nothing is sent anywhere.

sections.title: Update checks go to GitHub
sections.body: Owler checks for a new version once at launch. The check fetches one small file from GitHub Releases, so GitHub sees a request with your IP address, like any download. It carries nothing about your jobs.

sections.title: No analytics
sections.body: There are no crash reports, no usage tracking, no device IDs and no third-party SDKs in the app.

sections.title: About this website
sections.body: owler.kkweb.io, including this page, counts page views with Vercel Web Analytics. It uses no cookies and collects nothing that identifies you. What this page says about collecting nothing is about the app, not about these page view counts.

sections.title: You can check all of this
sections.body: Owler is open source under the MIT license. Everything on this page can be checked in the source code. If something looks wrong, open an issue.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: If a future version handles data differently, this page is updated before that version ships.
